v11.65 - u-101: satırlar tek kaynak, toplu profil ise gizli bir varsayılan değil bir eylem

The composer carried a "Delegation engine" box that read as a bulk switch over
the member rows and was not one: it wrote a mission-level FALLBACK, never
touched an existing row override, and had no model / effort / permission
counterpart. A user who set it and then looked at the rows saw the rows
disagreeing with it, and the same preference could be recorded in two places at
once. The box is gone, and the payload the UI posts no longer carries "engine".

In its place, in the Team/Pool heading: "Apply profile to included workers" —
engine, model, effort and permissions TOGETHER, written onto the rows in plain
sight. Three answers per dimension: don't change · inherit (clear the override)
· a value. That third one is the whole point: applying an ENGINE can no longer
wipe the models beside it, which is the accident a naive bulk apply makes every
time.

Every cell says whether it is an explicit override or an inherit — a left edge,
because the word does not fit in a 150px select and the AFTip already carries
the sentence.

‼️ And a value is no longer taken away without saying so. Moving a row onto an
engine that publishes neither its model nor its effort used to narrow it on the
spot: something somebody had typed vanished while their eyes were on a different
control, and the row afterwards gave no sign it had ever held one. The rows are
named ONCE in a strip offering "Clear them" or "Keep as they are", and a cleared
row afterwards says what went and why.

Found while wiring it: readProfile took an empty read at face value and would
have written '' onto a dimension the user had left alone — which is what "clear"
means and already has its own option. An empty read is now not an answer.

MissionSpec.engine is untouched: the bridge, every spec already on disk and
child-mission inheritance still use it and the resolver still reads it. This is
the UI declining to WRITE a second copy, not the contract losing a field.
